source: J. G. Telles Ribeiro and A. Cunha Jr, 'Scenario-driven optimization of passive vehicle suspensions: explaining the effectiveness of asymmetric damping', arXiv:2605.05235v1 (2026). Light vehicle of Table 2: ms 250 kg, mu 40 kg, kt 200000 N/m; fn 1.5 Hz, symmetric damping ratio 0.3 (Eqs. 14-15); ISO 8608 road (Table 1, Eq. 11, band 0.011 < n < 2.83 cycles/m) generated with a_i = sqrt(G_d(n_i) dn) (Eq. 13, half the ISO variance); v = 40 m/s; tire without tension (Eq. 8). Rft = sigma_Ft / ((ms + mu) g), Eq. 17.

tire_load_ratio.note: Section 3.2, Fig. 5 text: B 0.15 (no lift-off), C 0.30, D 0.53 (frequent lift-off)

minimum_tire_load_ratio.note: Section 4: the Rft-optimal designs at fn 1.5 Hz (B: 0.140 with sigma_aw 0.688 m/s^2; C: about 0.26 with sigma_aw 1.33 m/s^2). The paper optimizes bump and rebound damping separately.
